To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of emission of a 2.0 to 2.5 sec interresponse time is a function of the ratio between its frequency and the frequency of shorter interresponse times, the ratio being the reciprocal of the ratio between the frequency of shorter and longer interresponse times, and that this function is similar to that of the rate of emission for other operants.
the emission and the temporal distributions of an interresponse time vary as a function of its reinforcement schedule.
(1) the rate of emission of a 2-sec interresponse-time and (2) its temporal distribution vary as a function of reinforcement schedule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical problem in operant behavior, the problem of the reinforcement of interresponse time.
a class of schedules in which reinforcement is contingent upon the emission, rather than upon the rate of emission, of an interresponse time.
the analysis of the effects of reinforcement schedules on operants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interresponse time is an operant, that is, a response that can be modified by reinforcement, and that the interresponse times are differentially reinforced on different reinforcement schedules.
reinforcement of an interresponse time is a function of both the rate of emission of that interresponse time and its temporal distribution.

the reinforcement of an interresponse time is a function of the time of emission of the inter-response time, and that this time of emission is a function of its rate of emission, its temporal distribution, and the reinforcement contingency in effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interresponse time is an operant.
the reinforcement of interresponse time contingencies can be used to modify the rate of emission of the inter-response time and its temporal distribution.
the interresponse time behaves in a manner similar to other operants, and that the reinforcement of interresponse time schedules may be an important factor in the control of behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated that the reinforcement of interresponse time schedules is possible.
the interresponse time behaves like a response.
we can use reinforcement to change the distribution of interresponse times and that we can use interresponse times to change the distribution and the rate of reinforcement.
